children.text: hiraṇyaṃ hāṭakaṃ rukmaṃ suvarṇaṃ hema kāñcanam
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇya</s>, <s>hāṭaka</s>, <s>rukma</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, <s>hema</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s> are names of gold.
<s>Tapanīya</s>, <s>bhūricandra</s>, <s>kalyāṇa</s>, and <s>kaladhautaka</s> are also names.
<s>Cāmīkara</s>, <s>śātakumbha</s>, <s>surelaśa</s>, and <s>suvāsaka</s> are names of it.
<s>Jāmbūnada</s>, <s>bhūriniṣka</s>, <s>jātarūpa</s>, and <s>gairika</s> are also names.

children.text: svarṇaṃ kārtasvaraṃ bharma gāṅgeyaṃ kanakaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: <s>Svarṇa</s>, <s>kārtasvara</s>, <s>bharma</s>, <s>gāṅgeya</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, and <s>vasu</s> are names of gold.
<s>Aṣṭāpada</s>, <s>cārurūpa</s>, and <s>mahārajatakarbura</s> are further names.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ lekhanaṃ himam
children.translated_text: Gold is nourishing, aphrodisiac, astringent, scraping, cooling,
sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, bitter, good for the heart, heavy, and rejuvenating.
It gives strength, purity, benefit to the eyes, intellect, life, memory, and complexion.
It produces vigor and steadiness, purifies speech, and conquers
the three doṣas, wasting, insanity, abdominal enlargement, poison, and fever.
<s>Rajata</s>, <s>rucira</s>, <s>raupya</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, and <s>marupādaja</s> are names of silver.

children.text: śuddhaṃ kupyaṃ vasuśreṣṭhaṃ vimalaṃ śvetakaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddha</s>, <s>kupya</s>, <s>vasuśreṣṭha</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>śvetaka</s>, and <s>śiva</s> are also names.
<s>Saudha</s>, <s>tāra</s>, <s>taptarūpa</s>, <s>sitārāga</s>, and <s>mahāsudha</s> are further names.
<s>Candrahāsa</s>, <s>candravapuḥ</s>, <s>bāṣkala</s>, and <s>vahnibhūtika</s> are names of silver.
Silver is cooling, astringent and sour, sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, and mobile.
It preserves age, is unctuous and scraping, and conquers disorders of vāta and pitta.
<s>Tāmra</s>, <s>śulba</s>, <s>sarvaloha</s>, <s>tryambaka</s>, and <s>sarvavarcas</s> are names of copper.
<s>Dvyaṣṭa</s>, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, and <s>rakta</s>, shining like a lotus petal, are names.
<s>Audumbara</s>, <s>raktadhātu</s>, <s>kanīya</s>, and <s>sarvadhātuka</s> are also names.
<s>Naipālīya</s>, <s>ratnadhātu</s>, <s>mihira</s>, and <s>ravināmaka</s> are further names.

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktaṃ himaṃ svādu kaṣāyāmlaṃ saraṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Copper is bitter, cooling, sweet, astringent and sour, mobile, and light.
It is scraping, pungent in post-digestive effect, healing, and conquers kapha and pitta.
It destroys cough, skin disease, hemorrhoids, dyspnea, swelling, and pallor.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ lohanibhaṃ ghoṣaṃ prakāśaṃ kamalaṃ lavam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s>, resembling iron, is called <s>ghoṣa</s>, <s>prakāśa</s>, <s>kamala</s>, and <s>lava</s>.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ viśadaṃ saram ||
children.translated_text: Bronze is astringent, bitter, hot, scraping, clear, and mobile.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ guru kaphaṃ pittaṃ hanti dṛṣṭiprasādanam
children.translated_text: It is dry and heavy; it destroys kapha and pitta and clarifies the sight.
<s>Vartaloha</s>, <s>vaṭṭaloha</s>, <s>pañcaloha</s>, and <s>nīlikā</s> are names of this alloy.
<s>Varttaloha</s> is cooling, dry, pungent and sour, and conquers kapha and pitta.
<s>Pītaloha</s>, <s>varttaloha</s>, <s>triloha</s>, <s>saikya</s>, and <s>āraka</s> are names of brass.
<s>Ārakūṭa</s>, <s>rājarītī</s>, <s>rājñīrīti</s>, and <s>maheśvarī</s> are also names.
<s>Rīti</s> is bitter, cooling, dry, vāta-provoking, and conquers kapha and pitta.

children.text: raṅgaṃ vaṅgaṃ rūpaśaṃkhaṃ nighaṭaṃ piccaṭaṃ sitam
children.translated_text: <s>Raṅga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>rūpaśaṅkha</s>, <s>nighaṭa</s>, <s>piccaṭa</s>, and <s>sita</s> are names of tin.

children.text: śītaṃ trapukam ānīlaṃ kharaṭī nīlikā ghanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śīta</s>, <s>trapuka</s>, <s>ānīla</s>, <s>kharaṭī</s>, <s>nīlikā</s>, and <s>ghana</s> are further names.
<s>Guruśreṣṭha</s>, <s>salavaṇa</s>, <s>kastāra</s>, <s>vikaṭa</s>, and <s>rajas</s> are also names.
<s>Śīśa</s>, <s>bahumala</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>uraga</s>, <s>bhujaga</s>, and <s>guru</s> are names of lead.
<s>Yogeṣṭa</s>, <s>yavaneṣṭa</s>, <s>viśiṣṭa</s>, and <s>dhātuśodhana</s> are further names.
<s>Paripiṣṭa</s>, <s>vānapiṣṭa</s>, <s>pārvata</s>, and <s>dhātusambhava</s> are also names.
<s>Vapra</s>, <s>dhātumala</s>, <s>vaṅgamala</s>, <s>kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>mahābala</s> are names.

children.text: trapukaṃ tiktakaṃ bhedi laghūṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ paṭu ||
children.translated_text: Tin is bitter, purgative, light, hot, scraping, and sharp.
It is dry and beneficial to the eyes; it conquers kapha, dyspnea, pallor, kapha, and vāta.

children.text: mehaghnaṃ pittalaṃ kiṃcit tadvad vidyād bhujaṃgakam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys urinary disease and is somewhat pitta-producing; <s>bhujaṅgaka</s> should be known as similar.

children.text: ayaḥ kālāyasaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ piṇḍaṃ pāravasaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: <s>Ayaḥ</s>, <s>kālāyasa</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>pāravasa</s>, and <s>ghana</s> are names of iron.

children.text: lohaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ghanalohaṃ vīraṃ cīmaram āyasam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Loha</s>, <s>kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>ghanaloha</s>, <s>vīra</s>, <s>cīmara</s>, and <s>āyasa</s> are also names.
<s>Śastrakuṇṭha</s>, <s>aśmasāra</s>, <s>rakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>samayāntaka</s> are further names.

children.text: siṃhānaṃ lohaviṣṭhā tu maṇḍūraṃ syād ayomalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The excrement of iron is called <s>siṃhāna</s>; <s>maṇḍūra</s> is iron dross.
<s>Siṅghāṇaka</s>, <s>lohakiṭṭa</s>, <s>śastracūrṇa</s>, and <s>ayorajas</s> are names of iron filings or dross.

children.text: lohaṃ tiktaṃ saraṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: Iron is bitter, mobile, cooling, astringent, sweet, and heavy.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ vayasyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ lekhanaṃ vātalaṃ jayet
children.translated_text: It is dry, age-sustaining, beneficial to the eyes, scraping, vāta-provoking, and conquers
kapha, pitta, poison, colic, swelling, hemorrhoids, skin disease, and pallor.
It also conquers urinary disease, fat, and worms; its slag is similar, according to the type of iron.
Magnetite is sharp and cooling, and conquers urinary disease, vāta, and pallor.
It preserves age, is aphrodisiac, and conquers swelling, skin disease, and poison.
<s>Rasendra</s>, <s>pārada</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>hemabīja</s>, and <s>rajasvala</s> are names of mercury.
<s>Trilocana</s>, <s>hemanidhi</s>, <s>śivaputra</s>, and <s>rasottama</s> are also names.
<s>Rasaloha</s>, <s>lokanātha</s>, <s>jñānaretas</s>, and <s>mahānala</s> are further names.
Mercury destroys worms and skin disease, benefits the eyes, and is rejuvenating.
<s>Abhraka</s>, <s>abhrapaṭala</s>, <s>nirmala</s>, and <s>varapītaka</s> are names of mica.
<s>Medhāhva</s>, <s>pītaka</s>, <s>śubhra</s>, <s>girija</s>, and <s>girijāmala</s> are also names.

children.text: abhrakaṃ madhuraṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyaṃ guru dhātukṛt ||
children.translated_text: Mica is sweet, cooling, astringent, heavy, and productive of bodily elements.
It destroys the three doṣas, skin disease, wounds, urinary disease, poison, and worms.
<s>Vaigandha</s>, <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>gandhaka</s>, and <s>gandhamādana</s> are names of sulfur.
<s>Lelī</s>, <s>lelītaka</s>, <s>gandha</s>, <s>gandhāśman</s>, and <s>pītagandhaka</s> are also names.
<s>Vaṃśakāra</s>, <s>balivasā</s>, <s>varasaugandhika</s>, and <s>balin</s> are further names.
<s>Sūtaśatru</s>, <s>dhātumārī</s>, <s>śukapuṣpa</s>, and <s>vikṛtaka</s> are also names.
Sulfur is pungent and bitter; its potency is hot; it is astringent and mobile.
It increases pitta, is pungent in post-digestive effect, and removes itching, erysipelas, and skin disease.
It destroys kapha, vāta, wasting, spleen disease, and worms, and is rejuvenating.
<s>Tāpīja</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>madhudhātu</s>, and <s>śilāmadhu</s> are names of pyrite or mākṣika ore.
<s>Varta</s> and <s>mākṣikadhātu</s> are names; <s>saṃvarta</s> and <s>varamākṣika</s> are further names.
Another kind is born from silver, white, produced from silver, and resembling silver.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is astringent, bitter, sweet and sour, light, and pungent.

children.text: vyavāyī kaṭukaḥ pāke svaryo vṛṣyo rasāyanaḥ
children.translated_text: It is diffusive, pungent in post-digestive effect, good for the voice, aphrodisiac, and rejuvenating.
It benefits the eyes, is scraping, and destroys doṣas, skin disease, poison, and wasting.
It also destroys swelling, hemorrhoids, urinary disease, excessive urinary disorders, severe bleeding, abdominal enlargement, and pallor.

children.text: mākṣiko dvividhaḥ proktaḥ pītaḥ śuklastathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is said to be of two kinds: yellow and likewise white.
The excellent mineral <s>mākṣika</s> should be known as golden in color,
arising from the golden mountain; it is also called <s>viṣṇu</s> and <s>kāñcana</s>.
It is produced among the <s>Tāpī</s>, the <s>Kirātas</s>, the Chinese, and the Yavanas.
Called <s>tāpya</s>, it is seen in the month of <s>Mādhava</s>, heated by the rays of the sun.
It is sweet, with the appearance of gold; but when sour it resembles collyrium.

children.text: kiṃcit kaṣāya ubhayaḥ śītaḥ pāke kaṭurlaghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Both kinds are slightly astringent, cooling, pungent after digestion, and light.
In order, they are also bitter and hot; despite their sweetness they are scraping.
<s>Tāpya</s> is especially destructive of pallor, swelling, skin disease, and parasites.
It removes fever, cough, dyspnea, and diseases of the bladder, and it binds mercury.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is called <s>manoguptā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>nāgajihvikā</s>.

children.text: kucailā kunaṭī golā nepālā kavarī kalā
children.translated_text: It is <s>kucailā</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>golā</s>, <s>nepālā</s>, <s>kavarī</s>, and <s>kalā</s>.
It is also <s>śilā</s>, <s>nālī</s>, <s>nāgapuṣpā</s>, <s>pārthivī</s>, and <s>karavīrikā</s>.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is pungent and bitter, scraping, hot, heavy, and flowing.
It improves complexion, is unctuous, and removes kapha, dyspnea, cough, spirits, poison, and blood disorders.
<s>Haritāla</s> is called <s>āla</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>piñjara</s>, and <s>visragandhika</s>.
It is <s>pītaka</s>, <s>pītana</s>, <s>gaura</s>, <s>godana</s>, and <s>naramaṇḍana</s>.
It is <s>vaṅgāri</s>, <s>lohabhṛt</s>, <s>loma</s>, golden in appearance, and <s>viḍālaka</s>.

children.text: haritālaṃ kaṣāyoṣṇaṃ kaṭu snigdhaṃ hared viṣam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Haritāla</s> is astringent, hot, pungent, and unctuous; it removes poison.
It removes kapha and pitta disorders, mouth diseases, blood disorders, itching, skin disease, kapha, and wounds.
<s>Gairika</s> is called <s>girija</s>, <s>dhātu</s>, <s>girimṛt</s>, and <s>tvagavedhuka</s>.
<s>Gavedhuka</s> destroys worms; it is also <s>raktapāṣāṇaka</s>.
It is remembered as <s>raktadhātu</s>, <s>tāmradhātu</s>, <s>lohita</s>, and <s>kāraja</s>.
Another, resembling gold, is <s>svarṇagairika</s> and <s>svarṇabhūṣaṇa</s>.
It is good for the eyes, pacifies blood, is gentle to the blood, and rich in layers.
<s>Gairika</s> is sweet, unctuous, clear, astringent, and cooling.
It benefits the eyes and removes burning, nausea, kapha, pitta, and poison.
<s>Suvarṇagairika</s> is similar; it benefits the eyes and lessens vomiting and vāta.
<s>Tuttha</s> is <s>karparikātuttha</s> and also <s>amṛtāsaṅgama</s>.
Another kind is seen as <s>vitunnaka</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s>, and <s>hematāraka</s>.
Another is <s>mayūragrīvaka</s>; it is <s>kharpara</s> and <s>karparī</s>.

children.text: tutthakaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ viśadaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Tutthaka</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, clear, and light.
It is scraping, splitting, cooling, good for the eyes, and destructive of kapha and parasites.
It removes poison, stones, skin disease, and itching; <s>kārpara</s> is remembered as having the same qualities.
The <s>māyūra</s> kind resembles a peacock's neck and clarified butter or cow's milk.
When rubbed on iron together with sour juice, it becomes like copper.
It also floats on water: these are the marks of peacock-like <s>tuttha</s>.
That which resembles a dove or pigeon, and when broken has a brilliance like fire,
whose essence imitates silver, is the best <s>tuttha</s> for the eyes.
<s>Kāśīśa</s> is <s>dhātukāśīśa</s>, <s>śodhana</s>, and also <s>khecara</s>.
A second kind, <s>puṣpakāśīśa</s>, is hairy and impure.
<s>Kāśīśa</s> is sour, alkaline, astringent, hot, and beneficial for the eyes.
It is bitter, good for the hair, and removes poison, leucoderma, dysuria, stones, and kapha.
<s>Yātī</s>, <s>hiṅgulaka</s>, <s>rakta</s>, <s>pārvata</s>, and powdered mercury,
<s>maṇirāgakara</s>, <s>mleccha</s>, <s>gairika</s>, and <s>haṃsapādika</s>,
<s>atirakta</s>, <s>vālukita</s>, <s>saikata</s>, and <s>krauñcalohita</s>,
<s>darada</s>, <s>kuruvinda</s>, and another called <s>carmāravarcas</s> are names of it.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is light, bitter and hot; it is pungent and hot in taste and post-digestive effect.
It removes eye pain, skin disease, erysipelas, poison, pitta, and kapha.
<s>Śilāhva</s> is rock exudation; it is also <s>śilājatu</s> and <s>adrijatu</s>.
It is <s>jatvaśmaja</s>, <s>mandarottha</s>, <s>girija</s>, and <s>girisāhvaya</s>.
It should be known as arising from the six metals, as rock-dripping and mountain-born.
<s>Śilāhva</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, pungent after digestion, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
It is cutting and a <s>yogavāha</s> (catalytic carrier), and it destroys kapha, skin disease, stones, and pallor.
It also destroys gout, piles, worms, dyspnea, swelling, insanity, abdominal disease, and wasting.
<s>Raktareṇu</s>, <s>nāgagarbha</s>, splendid ornament of love,
<s>gandhārabhūṣaṇa</s>, red, <s>sindūra</s>, and lead-born,
<s>nāgarakta</s>, <s>vānapiṣṭa</s>, and adornment of the spring festival are names of it.
<s>Sindūra</s> is pungent and hot; it cleanses and heals wounds.
It joins fractures and defeats itching, poison, erysipelas, and skin disease.
<s>Suvīraja</s>, <s>kālanīla</s>, <s>raktasaṃvaraṇa</s>, and cooling,
<s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>mecaka</s>, black, <s>suvīra</s>, and <s>raktasaṃvara</s> are its names.
<s>Pārāvata</s>, mountain-born, <s>añjana</s>, and ornament of the eyes,

children.text: srotojaṃ yāmunaṃ nadyaṃ nadījaṃ nandanaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: <s>srotoja</s>, <s>yāmuna</s>, riverine, river-born, <s>nandana</s>, and excellent,
obtained by chance, desirable, <s>kāpota</s>, and ornament of the eyes are names of it.
Its form is like the peak of an anthill; when broken, it resembles collyrium.
When rubbed, it has the appearance of <s>gairika</s>; this is the mark of <s>srotoja</s>.

children.text: sauvīraṃ madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ lekhanaṃ himam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvīra</s> is sweet, unctuous, astringent, scraping, and cooling.
It conquers hiccup, dyspnea, poison, vomiting, kapha, pitta, wasting, and blood disorders.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ pravaraṃ grāhi tadvat srotoñjanaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: It is excellent for the eyes and constipating; <s>srotoñjana</s> is considered similar.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, <s>rasagarbha</s>, and <s>rasottama</s>.
It is <s>rasāgrya</s>, <s>tārkṣyaja</s>, and <s>tārkṣya</s>; another comes from the essence of <s>dārvī</s>.
The artificial kind made from <s>dārvī</s> and the like is <s>dārvya</s>, <s>rasaja</s>, and a medicine for children.
<s>Rasaja</s> is pungent, bitter, hot in potency, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
It destroys kapha, is cutting and good for wounds, and overcomes disorders of the mouth and eyes.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is <s>rītipuṣpa</s>, <s>kausuma</s>, and <s>kusumāñjana</s>.
It is <s>parīti</s>, <s>rītija</s>, <s>puṣpa</s>, <s>puṣpaketu</s>, and <s>pauṣpaka</s>.
<s>Rītija</s> is light and alkaline, and removes cataract, pterygium, and films over the eye.
<s>Mṛtsā</s>, <s>mṛtsnā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>saṅgā</s>, <s>jitākāśī</s>, and <s>mṛttikā</s>
as well as that born in <s>Surāṣṭra</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, excellent earth, and <s>mṛtālaka</s>, are its names.
<s>Āḍhakī</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>kāṃkṣī</s>, <s>sujātā</s>, and purifier of gold
are names of <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>. It is pungent, bitter, astringent, and hot, and it checks
kapha, pitta, poison, vitiligo, itching, wounds, and erysipelas.
Black earth is praised for wounds, burning, bleeding, and pradarā discharge.
Mud is cooling and unctuous, and conquers poison, pitta, blood-disorders, and fractures.
It removes swelling, burning, and wounds, and is beneficial for cleansing and healing.
It benefits the hair, is like elephant ichor, colors vitiligo, and destroys poison.

children.text: bolaṃ jātīrasaṃ pauraṃ nirlohaṃ barbaraṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bola</s>, <s>jātīrasa</s>, <s>paura</s>, <s>nirloha</s>, <s>barbara</s>, and <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: rasagandhaṃ ca gandhāmnaṃ gomataṃ nālikaṃ balam
children.translated_text: also <s>rasagandha</s>, <s>gandhāmna</s>, <s>gomata</s>, <s>nālika</s>, <s>bala</s>,
<s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>stoka</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, <s>stomaka</s>, and <s>vāsagandhaka</s> are its names.

children.text: bolastiktaḥ kaṭuḥ svāduḥ pācano dīpano himaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bola</s> is bitter, pungent, and sweet; it digests, kindles appetite, and is cooling.
It promotes intelligence and virility, removes the three doṣas, and cleanses the womb.
It destroys epilepsy, skin disease, piles, fractures, disorders of sweating, seizure, and fever.
<s>Gorocanā</s> is called <s>vandanīyā</s>, <s>vandanī</s>, <s>rucirā</s>, and <s>ruci</s>;

children.text: maṅgalyā gautamī gaurī bhogyā rucyā ca pācanī
children.translated_text: also <s>maṅgalyā</s>, <s>gautamī</s>, <s>gaurī</s>, <s>bhogyā</s>, <s>rucyā</s>, and <s>pācanī</s>.

children.text: medhyā gopittajā vaśyā piṅgalā rocanā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It is intellect-promoting, born from cow-bile, subduing, tawny, and remembered as <s>rocanā</s>.
<s>Gorocanā</s> is cooling, bitter, dry, and gives auspiciousness and beauty.
It removes poison, inauspiciousness, seizure by spirits, madness, miscarriage, wounds, and bleeding.

children.text: śaileyaṃ sthaviraṃ vṛddhaṃ śailajaṃ palitaṃ gṛham
children.translated_text: <s>Śaileya</s>, <s>sthavira</s>, <s>vṛddha</s>, <s>śailaja</s>, <s>palita</s>, and <s>gṛha</s>,
<s>śilāpuṣpa</s>, <s>śilādadru</s>, <s>jīrṇa</s>, and <s>kālānusāryaka</s> are its names.
<s>Śaileya</s> is cooling, tasty, light, and removes kapha and fever.
It destroys poison, burning, blood-disorders, itching, skin disease, stone, and heart disease.
<s>Saṃdhināla</s>, <s>kararuha</s>, <s>karaja</s>, <s>nakhara</s>, and <s>khara</s>;
also conch, horse-hoof, oyster shell, artisan's shell, elephant jaw, and jaw;
<s>badarīchadana</s>, <s>kāśī</s>, and another, <s>haṭṭavilāsinī</s>;
that born from a tiger is <s>vyāghranakha</s>, the tiger's claw, the weapon of a beast, the nail.
It is born from a tiger's foot, tiger-palm, <s>kūṭastha</s>, and <s>cakrakāraka</s>.
<s>Śārdūla</s>, <s>paurasa</s>, <s>paura</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>niloha</s>, and <s>barbara</s> are further names.
The two kinds of nail are light and sweet, pungent in taste and post-digestive effect,

children.text: tiktoṣṇaṃ śukralaṃ varṇyaṃ hṛdyaṃ hanti kaphānilau ||
children.translated_text: bitter, hot, semen-promoting, complexion-promoting, and cordial; they remove kapha and wind.
They remove poison, skin disease, disorders of nails and sweat, bad odor, tears, seizure, and fever.
<s>Saindhava</s>, <s>rucaka</s>, black salt, <s>viḍa</s>, sea salt, <s>audbhida</s>,
<s>romaka</s>, and earth-born salt: these are called the eight salts.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ sarvaṃ pācanaṃ rocanaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: All salt, as salt, is digestive, appetite-producing, and softening.
It is sweet, promotes the discharge of feces and urine, is both unctuous and dry, and diminishes strength.
Hot in potency, appetite-kindling, sharp, it increases kapha and pitta.
It is burning, heavy, clogging, and conquers abdominal tumors, upward movement of wind, and pain.
Among them <s>saindhava</s> is the best, sweet in taste and post-digestive effect.

children.text: saindhavaṃ sindhu sindhūtthaṃ nādeyaṃ vimalaṃ varam
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s>, <s>sindhu</s>, <s>sindhūttha</s>, <s>nādeya</s>, spotless, excellent,

children.text: śivaṃ śītaśivaṃ śuddhaṃ sindhujaṃ lavaṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: auspicious, cool-auspicious, pure, born from the Sindhu, and supreme salt are its names.
Rock-like, <s>maṇimantha</s>, <s>dhauteya</s>, and the finest condiment are further names.

children.text: saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ svādu dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> salt is sweet, appetite-kindling, digestive, and light.

children.text: snigdhaṃ rucyaṃ himaṃ vṛṣyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ netryaṃ tridoṣahṛt
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, tasty, cooling, virility-promoting, subtle, beneficial to the eyes, and removes the three doṣas.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> is remembered as having a pleasant odor, fragrant, and <s>rucaka</s>.

children.text: saugandhikaṃ ca jaraṇam akṣam anyad agandhikam
children.translated_text: It is also <s>saugandhika</s>, digestive, <s>akṣa</s>; another kind is without smell.

children.text: rucakaṃ rocanaṃ hṛdyaṃ dīpanaṃ viśadaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rucaka</s> is appetite-producing, cordial, appetite-kindling, clear, and light.
Hot in potency and pungent in post-digestive effect, it purifies fragrant belching.
It is slightly unctuous, pungent, sharp, subtle, and removes pain and constipation.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ ca kṛṣṇalavaṇaṃ mecakaṃ tilakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Black salt, <s>kṛṣṇalavaṇa</s>, <s>mecaka</s>, and <s>tilaka</s> are its names.
In black salt the qualities of <s>sauvarcala</s> are present, except for fragrance.
<s>Viḍa</s>-smelling salt, cookable salt, <s>ghaṭikālavaṇa</s>, and <s>viḍa</s>;
also artificial salt, chunk salt, Dravidian salt, deceitful salt, and demonic salt are its names.
<s>Viḍa</s>, because it has alkali, guides kapha and vāta downward and upward in the proper direction.

children.text: dīpanaṃ laghu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ rucyaṃ vyavāyi ca ||
children.translated_text: It is appetite-kindling, light, sharp, hot, dry, tasty, and diffusive.
It removes constipation, distension, obstruction, heart disease, heaviness, and pain.
Sea salt is <s>sāmudraka</s>, produced from the ocean, pungent, and ocean-born salt.
Sea salt is <s>sāmudralavaṇa</s>, <s>akṣīva</s>, <s>trikūṭa</s>, and water-born.

children.text: sāmudraṃ madhuraṃ pāke satiktaṃ kaṭukaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: Sea salt is sweet in post-digestive effect, slightly bitter, pungent, and heavy.
It is not excessively hot, kindles appetite, breaks accumulations, contains alkali, and is not burning.
Very unctuous and sweet, it removes vāta, increases phlegm, and does not greatly increase pitta.
<s>Audbhida</s>, earthy, <s>caurya</s>, earth-arisen, and earth-born are its names.
It is produced from alkaline water that has arisen by breaking out of the earth and then been dried
by sun-rays or by fire, or by boiling; thus <s>audbhida</s> is pungent.
<s>Audbhida</s> is sharp, nauseating, alkaline, pungent, and bitter.
It affects the blood, is light, sharp, hot, subtle, and sets vāta in its proper course.
Another is <s>romalavaṇa</s>, also called <s>romaka</s> and <s>vastaka</s>.
<s>Romaka</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, light, clogging, and diuretic.

children.text: vātaghnaṃ tīkṣṇamatyuṣṇaṃ bhedi sūkṣmaṃ vyavāyi ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes vāta, is sharp, excessively hot, breaking, subtle, and diffusive.
<s>Pāṃśuja</s>, <s>pāṃśulavaṇa</s>, <s>pāṃśuka</s>, and excellent <s>vasuka</s> are its names.

children.text: ūṣakakṣāram aurvaṃ syād auṣaṃ sarvaguṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: It may be called <s>ūṣakakṣāra</s>, <s>aurva</s>, or <s>auṣa</s>; it has all the qualities.

children.text: pāṃśukaṃ kaṭukaṃ snigdhaṃ sakṣāraṃ śleṣmalaṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṃśuka</s> is pungent, unctuous, alkaline, phlegm-producing, and heavy.

children.text: kācaṃ pākyaṃ trikūṭaṃ syātsarvaṃ tu lavaṇaṃ kaṭu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāca</s>, <s>pākya</s>, and <s>trikūṭa</s> are its names; every salt, however, is pungent.
<s>Kāca</s> is alkaline and hot, and is beneficial for the eyes when used as collyrium.
Guṭikā-lavaṇa is purgative, kindles digestion, and provokes pitta.
It is considered to destroy kapha, vāta, and worms, to scrape, and to digest.
Maulākāra, cārukaila, and auṣa by name are cutting and pungent.
With sindhu, sauvarcala, viḍa, sāmudra, udbhida, and romaka salts,
together with sapāṃśu and black salt, the salts are successively counted as two, three, and so on.
But in the application of salts one should use saindhava and the others in order.
Yavakṣāra is also called yāvaśūka, yavāhva, and yāvanālaja.
It is śūkapāka, śūkaja, yavaja, and yavaśūkaja.
The alkali is pākyas, sharp in taste, yāvya, pāka, and yavāgraja.
Yavakṣāra is light, unctuous, very subtle, and kindles the digestive fire.
It destroys kapha, vāta, āma, dyspnea, colic, and diseases of the throat.
It also destroys abdominal tumors, piles, grahaṇī disorder, spleen disease, anemia, distension, and heart disease.
Svarjikā is svarjikākṣāra, sukhavarca, and suvarcikā.
This alkali, suvarcikā and pākyā, is remembered as srotoghnī and potaka.
Svarjikākṣāra is said to have qualities only slightly different from it.
Yavakṣāra, that called svarjikā, ṭaṅkaṇa, and that born from sesame stalks,
and those produced from palāśa, kadalī, moca, śvadaṃṣṭrā, mokṣaka, and the like,
all alkalis are like fire; they cut, purge, and tear apart.
They are hot in potency, saline, sharp, moistening, and burning.
They kindle appetite, digest, are dry and clear, and give rise to blood-pitta.
They injure semen, vigor, hair, and sight; they are pungent, strong, and flowing.
Unpleasant to the heart, they destroy abdominal tumors, piles, gravel, urinary stones, and chronic catarrh.
They also destroy constipation, distension, anemia, balāsa, grahaṇī disorder, and worms.
Ṭaṅkaṇa and ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra arise from the juice of mālatī.
Ṭaṅkaṇa purifies iron, liquefies, and digests everything.
Ṭaṅkaṇa kindles digestion, is dry, destroys phlegm, and produces vāta and pitta.
Uṣakṣāra is siṃhamūtra, mūṣaka, and kṣāramṛttikā.
Uṣakṣāra, originating from urine, destroys hair, vāta, and strength.
It is moistening, pungent in digestion, hot in potency, and produces blood-pitta.
The alkali is declared to be emetic, to destroy fat, and to cleanse the bladder.
Śvādaṃṣṭrā is said to be sweet, cooling, and cleansing to the channels.
Palāśa is best in actions and in all respects free from danger.
Hiṇḍīra, ocean-kapha, foam, likewise water-kapha, and ocean-born,
dry or undried, water-impurity, water-foam, and ocean-foam are its names.

children.text: abdhipheno laghuḥ śītaḥ kaṣāyo lekhano jayet ||
children.translated_text: Ocean-foam is light, cooling, astringent, and scraping; it conquers
white eye growth, films, phlegm, pitta, ear disease, and poison.
Śaṅkha, the conch, is water-moving, kambu, water-born, and long-resounding.
It is well-sounding, long-toned, white, and an ornament of <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: śaṃkho'nuṣṇaḥ kaṭuḥ pāke kaṣāyo madhuro laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Conch is not hot, pungent in digestion, astringent, sweet, and light.
It benefits the eyes, scrapes, and conquers indigestion, colic, pitta, kapha, and blood disorders.
Small conches are known as śaṅkhanaka, śambūka, and kṣullaka.
They are carācara, varāṭa, kaparda, and water-shells.
They are muktāsphoṭa, ocean-frog, śukti, and jewel-house.
Śambūka promotes the discharge of feces and urine, is sweet, and removes diseases of pitta.
The small conch is like that; conch in particular is moistening and heavy.
Shells remove pitta, promote the discharge of feces and urine, and are beneficial for the eyes.
Hīraka, bhidura, vajra, chief jewel, and varāṭaka,
sūcīmukha and kuliśa, gomeda and pītaraktaka,
aśmayoni, nīlamaṇi, vaidūrya, and bālavāyaja,
pravāla, vahnikāgra, vidruma, and raktavarṇaka,
sūryakānta, vahnimaṇi, arkāhva, and dahanopala,
candropala, candrakānta, sphaṭika, and sphaṭikopala,
māṇikya, śasyaka, and likewise the jewel vasumaṇi are to be known.
Pautika, mauktika, muktā, and muktāphala arise from essence.
Gārutmata, marakata, aśmagarbha, and harinmaṇi are names of emerald.
Vajra, padmarāga, indranīla, vaidūrya, and vidruma,
the sun-stone and moon-stone gems, pearl, emerald, and the rest,
are astringent, sweet, cooling, good for the eyes, scraping, and flowing.
When worn they are auspicious and remove sin, misfortune, and poison.
Rājāvarta is a black gem, golden in luster and densely shining.
Rājavartaka destroys urinary disorders, vomiting, and disease.
Vaikrānta, equal in qualities to diamond, is pleasing to the heart and destroys poison.
It removes skin disease, wasting, and fever, and is remembered as producing bodily and metallic firmness.
Maṅkolūka, mineral ore, dark-white, white, and chalk,
and another called nāḍītaraṅgaka, white and pale, are remembered.
Chalk is sweet and conquers swelling, poison, burning, and blood disorders.
Another is called kṣīrapāka, and another is considered to be sudhāpāṣāṇaka.
Kārā, made of various minerals, is known as vālukā and sikatā, sand.
It is enticing, mother of the world, subtle, and born from gold.
